title: Falling ball

source.credit: Rendered by Ansatz with exactly known physics (restitution e = 0.72)

slow_motion.evidence: no narration, captions, or on-screen text indicate slow motion

subjects.description: small orange spherical ball falling vertically

observation.what_happens: An orange ball drops from just below a black-and-white scale bar at the top to the brown floor at the bottom. The motion starts at release near the top and ends when the ball reaches the floor.

calibration.note: scale from the fall itself: 3275 px/s² over 6 arcs = g of 9.807 m/s²

given: g = 9.807 m/s² (Earth); it set the scale, so treat g as known and fixed
reasoning: x drifts steadily while y makes repeated parabolic arcs hitting about -1.44 m and rebounding lower each time, so this is a bouncing ball under gravity. Air on Earth may add small drag, and the bounce needs restitution and possibly horizontal loss, so we test vacuum vs linear vs quadratic drag with bounce events.

law.title: Bouncing ball in vacuum
law.summary: The ball falls under gravity and bounces off the floor losing the same fraction of bounce each time.

headline: Falling ball bounces in vacuum with no air drag.
finding: The ball falls under gravity with 9.81 m/s² and hits the floor at -1.44 ± 0.004 m, then bounces keeping 0.72 ± 0.00034 of its speed.

eyeball.law_in_words: Free fall under gravity calibrated by the 1m black-white reference bar; normal restitution is rebound over impact vertical speed, zero because no upward rebound is seen and the ball embeds below the floor surface.
